Results.ReviewText: After 12 years with the last one, we needed a need a new, reliable gas grill. The kids have moved out, we don't have the parties and bbq's that we used to have. The large grill with the side burners and charring burner is no longer needed. We store the the grill in the garage and roll it when used, which is still 2-3 times a week. So smaller and lighter was preferred. Friends and family have sworn by the Weber name so we gave it a try. The E-210 is perfect! Smaller, lighter and still a LOT of grilling area. It was a great purchase and highly recommended. Not quite sure how the gas gage/weight system works and installing a new filled tank is tricky, but still love it.

Results.ReviewText: I retired my Weber grill and purchased the Spirit E210 as a replacement about one month ago. This unit performs perfectly and is used frequently. The E210 comes equipped with a built in scale for the propane tank, so you are constantly aware of the fuel supply status.

ClientResponses.Response:
Your feedback means a lot to us. We are very sorry to hear your grill cabinet is rusting. We are here to help. 

If your grill is located in a coastal or humid area, or if chlorine is present in your environment, additional maintenance will be needed to keep up the appearance of the exterior steel parts. 

Click here to watch a quick video on how to clean the exterior of your grill. 

Also, below are a couple helpful tips. 

1. At the first sign of staining/discoloration/surface rust we would recommend cleaning with stainless steel cleaner (ex. Bar Keepers Friend). Once cleaned, we recommend using a stainless steel polish (ex. Weber's brand) to keep it looking its best in-between cleanings.

2. Once a week we would recommend wiping down the grill with a wet towel or rag and then drying completely.

3. We would only recommend covering your grill if you know inclement weather is coming.

4. The quicker you get at a stain the easier it will be to clean off.

Please look for an outreach email from us soon. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText: We got this grill after doing some research.  It looks good, haven't used yet.  The reason why we haven't used it yet is because this grill does does NOT allow you to place the propane on the interior of the cart.  The hole for the propane is way too big- the propane tank just falls through.  We even put a board over the hole, but then the tank won't fit into the storage area.  Supposedly, the tank is to be placed on this side hanger gadget which on the side wall of the cabinet.  Need to take some time to figure out how that works.  It is NOT a simple- hang the tank and go-hook.  If I would have known this, I would have purchased a different grill.
Results.Title: Not happy having to HANGE the propane tank...

Results.ReviewText: This little guy packs a lot in one small grill! Both burners offer plenty of grilling space plus a cross burner allows for Long fish and sirloins to grill sideways, unique weight hanger tells you the amount of fuel left in the tank, side trays fold for easy storing, and the thermometer is as good as their top line grills. My last huge Weber grill lasted over 11 years and was still going and a part of the sale of my old house! Choose the weber grill you want and expect to keep it a lifetime. My friends are all on their 4-5th grill. Pay the money once up front and never buy another grill or by cheap and pay for a new grill over and over again. Most of my friends have already paid more for their many grills than I paid for my one grill and the others are catching up. Weber's sales slogan should be one and done!
Results.Title: Buy a weber= one and done!
